title: Impact of Short Sale Ban on Financial Stock Volatility

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Difference-in-Differences with unit and period fixed effects (two-way FE).
- Why: The ban applies to a subset of financial stocks (treated) at a common time (post). DID compares the change in log volatility for treated stocks before vs. after the ban to the contemporaneous change for non-treated stocks, netting out time-invariant stock characteristics and common time shocks.
- Key assumptions:
  - Parallel trends: In the absence of the ban, treated and control stocks’ log volatility would have followed the same trend.
  - No spillovers: The ban on treated stocks does not directly affect the volatility of control stocks.
  - Stable composition and timing: No systematic entry/exit around the ban that differs by group; ban timing not anticipatorily targeted at stocks with changing volatility trends.
  - SUTVA: Potential outcomes for a stock depend only on its own treatment status.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Complete, self-contained R code

# 1) Setup ------------------------------------------------------------------
req_pkgs <- c("fixest", "dplyr")
for (p in req_pkgs) {
  if (!requireNamespace(p, quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages(p, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
  }
}
library(fixest)
library(dplyr)

# 2) Read data --------------------------------------------------------------
df <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s43_data.csv")

# Basic checks
stopifnot(all(c("unit_id","period","treated","post","treat_x_post","y") %in% names(df)))
df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    unit_id = as.factor(unit_id),
    period = as.integer(period),
    treated = as.integer(treated),
    post = as.integer(post),
    treat_x_post = as.integer(treat_x_post),
    y = as.numeric(y)
  )

# Determine the ban period (first period with post==1)
if (!any(df$post == 1)) stop("No post-ban periods found (post==1).")
ban_period <- min(df$period[df$post == 1], na.rm = TRUE)
ref_period <- ban_period - 1

cat("Ban period identified as:", ban_period, "with reference (last pre) period:", ref_period, "\n")

# 3) Baseline DID with two-way fixed effects --------------------------------
# DID estimate of treatment effect on log volatility
mod_baseline <- feols(
  y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period,
  data = df,
  cluster = ~ unit_id # cluster at stock level
)

b <- coef(mod_baseline)["treat_x_post"]
se_b <- se(mod_baseline)["treat_x_post"]
ci_b <- confint(mod_baseline, "treat_x_post", level = 0.95)
p_b <- coeftable(mod_baseline)["treat_x_post", "Pr(>|t|)"]

cat("\nBaseline DID (cluster by unit):\n")
cat(sprintf("  Coef (treat_x_post) = %.4f, SE = %.4f, 95%% CI = [%.4f, %.4f], p-val = %.4f\n",
            b, se_b, ci_b[1], ci_b[2], p_b))

# 4) Robustness: Two-way clustering (unit and period) -----------------------
mod_twocluster <- feols(
  y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period,
  data = df,
  cluster = ~ unit_id + period
)
b2 <- coef(mod_twocluster)["treat_x_post"]
se_b2 <- se(mod_twocluster)["treat_x_post"]
ci_b2 <- confint(mod_twocluster, "treat_x_post", level = 0.95)
p_b2 <- coeftable(mod_twocluster)["treat_x_post", "Pr(>|t|)"]

cat("\nRobustness 1: Two-way clustered SE (unit and period):\n")
cat(sprintf("  Coef (treat_x_post) = %.4f, SE = %.4f, 95%% CI = [%.4f, %.4f], p-val = %.4f\n",
            b2, se_b2, ci_b2[1], ci_b2[2], p_b2))

# 5) Robustness: Group-specific linear trend --------------------------------
# Add a treated-specific linear time trend
df <- df %>% mutate(trend = as.numeric(period))
mod_trend <- feols(
  y ~ treat_x_post + treated:trend | unit_id + period,
  data = df,
  cluster = ~ unit_id + period
)
b3 <- coef(mod_trend)["treat_x_post"]
se_b3 <- se(mod_trend)["treat_x_post"]
ci_b3 <- confint(mod_trend, "treat_x_post", level = 0.95)
p_b3 <- coeftable(mod_trend)["treat_x_post", "Pr(>|t|)"]

cat("\nRobustness 2: Add treated-specific linear trend:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Coef (treat_x_post) = %.4f, SE = %.4f, 95%% CI = [%.4f, %.4f], p-val = %.4f\n",
            b3, se_b3, ci_b3[1], ci_b3[2], p_b3))

# 6) Event-study style pre-trend check --------------------------------------
# Interact treated with period dummies, reference = last pre-ban period
# This yields dynamic effects for treated vs controls by period, relative to ref.
if (any(df$period == ref_period)) {
  mod_es <- feols(
    y ~ i(period, treated, ref = ref_period) | unit_id + period,
    data = df,
    cluster = ~ unit_id + period
  )
  cn <- names(coef(mod_es))
  # Coefficients look like "period::k#treated"
  is_treat_dyn <- grepl("^period::", cn) & grepl("#treated", cn)
  # Extract the numeric period from the name
  per_num <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(sub("period::(-?\\d+)#treated", "\\1", cn)))
  lead_names <- cn[is_treat_dyn & per_num < ref_period & !is.na(per_num)]

  cat("\nEvent-study pre-trend test (joint H0: all pre-period effects = 0):\n")
  if (length(lead_names) >= 1) {
    H <- paste0(lead_names, " = 0")
    w <- fixest::wald(mod_es, H)
    # Print F-stat and p-value
    if (!is.null(w$stat) && !is.null(w$p.value)) {
      cat(sprintf("  F-stat = %.3f, p-val = %.4f, df = (%s)\n",
                  w$stat, w$p.value,
                  if (!is.null(w$df)) paste(w$df, collapse = ",") else "NA"))
    } else {
      print(w)
    }
  } else {
    cat("  Not enough pre-periods to conduct a lead test (no leads relative to reference).\n")
  }
} else {
  cat("\nEvent-study skipped: reference period not present in data.\n")
}

# 7) Placebo test in pre-periods only ---------------------------------------
# Pretend the ban happened one period earlier; estimate DID within true pre-sample
placebo_cut <- ref_period
pre_df <- df %>% filter(period <= placebo_cut)
if (nrow(pre_df) > 0 && any(pre_df$period == placebo_cut)) {
  pre_df <- pre_df %>%
    mutate(fake_post = as.integer(period >= placebo_cut),
           fake_treat_post = treated * fake_post)
  mod_placebo <- feols(
    y ~ fake_treat_post | unit_id + period,
    data = pre_df,
    cluster = ~ unit_id + period
  )
  bp <- coef(mod_placebo)["fake_treat_post"]
  sep <- se(mod_placebo)["fake_treat_post"]
  cip <- confint(mod_placebo, "fake_treat_post", level = 0.95)
  pp <- coeftable(mod_placebo)["fake_treat_post", "Pr(>|t|)"]

  cat("\nPlacebo DID (pre-periods only, pseudo-ban at last pre period):\n")
  cat(sprintf("  Coef (fake_treat_post) = %.4f, SE = %.4f, 95%% CI = [%.4f, %.4f], p-val = %.4f\n",
              bp, sep, cip[1], cip[2], pp))
} else {
  cat("\nPlacebo test skipped: insufficient pre-period observations.\n")
}

# 8) Final clear numerical result -------------------------------------------
cat("\n=== Final Result (Preferred spec: Two-way FE with two-way clustered SE) ===\n")
cat(sprintf("Treatment effect on log volatility (treat_x_post): %.4f\n", b2))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Positive. Short-sale bans typically reduce price discovery and market-making by short sellers, worsening liquidity and potentially amplifying volatility; thus, treated stocks’ log volatility should rise relative to controls after the ban.
- Magnitude: An increase in log volatility on the order of 0.05 to 0.20 (about 5%–22%), consistent with documented rises in volatility and trading frictions around historical short-sale bans.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare changes in log stock volatility between treated and untreated stocks before and after the ban.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The short selling ban led to a reduction in log stock volatility for the treated financial stocks.
